metadata.publication_policy: Nothing in this catalog is student-visible until editorial and pronunciation statuses are approved. Listening resources are not playable until a real audio asset has been generated, checked and attached.
metadata.breaking_change: This v2 replaces the three pre-1.4 seed JSON files, their category names, A0 level alias, importer and heuristic phonetic engine. No legacy aliases are maintained.

Names, personal information and basic self-description

lexical_items.definition_en: A basic question used to ask someone's name.

examples.english_text: What's your name? My name is Ana.

lexical_items.definition_en: A simple frame for giving your name.
A simple frame for saying where you come from.
A direct request for assistance.
A basic way to signal a comprehension problem.
A request for slower speech.

examples.english_text: Please speak slowly. I'm learning English.
examples.spanish_translation: Por favor, habla despacio. Estoy aprendiendo inglés.

lexical_items.definition_en: A common collocation for the first meal of the day.
A common phrase for shopping as an activity.
A polite frame for ordering or requesting something.

examples.english_text: I'd like a glass of water, please.
examples.spanish_translation: Quisiera un vaso de agua, por favor.

lexical_items.definition_en: To ask someone how to get to a place.

examples.english_text: We asked for directions near the station.
examples.spanish_translation: Pedimos indicaciones cerca de la estación.

lexical_items.definition_en: To arrange a time to meet a professional or service.

examples.english_text: I need to make an appointment with the doctor.
examples.spanish_translation: Necesito pedir una cita con el médico.

lexical_items.definition_en: Used to refer to Monday through Friday.
To arrange a table, room or service in advance.

examples.english_text: We made a reservation for two at the hotel.
examples.spanish_translation: Hicimos una reserva para dos en el hotel.

lexical_items.definition_en: To stop an activity for a short time.

examples.english_text: Let's take a short break after this lesson.
examples.spanish_translation: Tomemos un descanso corto después de esta lección.

lexical_items.definition_en: To take care of a person, animal or thing.

examples.english_text: She looks after her younger brother after school.
examples.spanish_translation: Ella cuida a su hermano menor después de la escuela.

lexical_items.definition_en: To use all of something and have none left.

examples.english_text: We ran out of milk, so I went to the shop.
examples.spanish_translation: Nos quedamos sin leche, así que fui a la tienda.

lexical_items.definition_en: To prepare yourself for an activity or event.

examples.english_text: I get ready before I leave for work.
examples.spanish_translation: Me preparo antes de salir al trabajo.

lexical_items.definition_en: To discover information by asking or checking.

examples.english_text: I called the office to find out the opening hours.
examples.spanish_translation: Llamé a la oficina para averiguar el horario.

lexical_items.definition_en: To be responsible for a person, task or thing.

examples.english_text: Can you take care of the tickets?

lexical_items.definition_en: To take action to manage a task, issue or situation.

examples.english_text: The team needs to deal with the customer complaint.
examples.spanish_translation: El equipo debe ocuparse de la queja del cliente.

lexical_items.definition_en: To participate in an event or activity.

examples.english_text: Several students took part in the discussion.
examples.spanish_translation: Varios estudiantes participaron en la discusión.

lexical_items.definition_en: To arrange something or make it ready for use; sense depends on context.

examples.english_text: We set up a meeting for Monday.
examples.spanish_translation: Organizamos una reunión para el lunes.

lexical_items.definition_en: To perform or complete a task, plan or investigation.

examples.english_text: The researchers carried out a short survey.
examples.spanish_translation: Los investigadores llevaron a cabo una encuesta breve.

lexical_items.definition_en: To delay an event or task until later.

examples.english_text: They put off the meeting because two people were ill.
examples.spanish_translation: Pospusieron la reunión porque dos personas estaban enfermas.

lexical_items.definition_en: To improve or move forward toward a goal.

examples.english_text: She is making progress with her listening skills.
examples.spanish_translation: Está progresando en su comprensión auditiva.

lexical_items.definition_en: To contact someone to ask, offer or discuss something.

examples.english_text: I will reach out to the supplier this afternoon.
examples.spanish_translation: Me pondré en contacto con el proveedor esta tarde.

lexical_items.definition_en: To consider a fact when making a decision.

examples.english_text: We must take the delivery time into account.
examples.spanish_translation: Debemos tener en cuenta el tiempo de entrega.

lexical_items.definition_en: To finish work by the agreed date or time.

examples.english_text: The team worked together to meet the deadline.
examples.spanish_translation: El equipo trabajó en conjunto para cumplir el plazo.

lexical_items.definition_en: To think of an idea, plan or solution.

examples.english_text: She came up with a practical alternative.

lexical_items.definition_en: To take further action after an earlier discussion or request.

examples.english_text: I will follow up on the proposal tomorrow.
examples.spanish_translation: Haré seguimiento de la propuesta mañana.

lexical_items.definition_en: To formally or clearly mention a possible problem.

examples.english_text: The reviewer raised a concern about the timeline.
examples.spanish_translation: La persona revisora planteó una preocupación sobre el cronograma.

lexical_items.definition_en: To achieve a shared decision after discussion.

examples.english_text: Both sides reached an agreement on the new schedule.
examples.spanish_translation: Ambas partes llegaron a un acuerdo sobre el nuevo horario.

lexical_items.definition_en: To share the latest information about progress or status.

examples.english_text: Please provide an update before the client meeting.
examples.spanish_translation: Por favor, comparte una actualización antes de la reunión con el cliente.

lexical_items.definition_en: To use evidence as the basis for an explanation or decision.

examples.english_text: The report draws on evidence from several independent studies.
examples.spanish_translation: El informe se apoya en evidencia de varios estudios independientes.

lexical_items.definition_en: To decide that an option is not possible or suitable.

examples.english_text: The budget rules out the most expensive option.
examples.spanish_translation: El presupuesto descarta la opción más costosa.

lexical_items.definition_en: To explain why a difference exists.

examples.english_text: The sample size may account for the difference in results.
examples.spanish_translation: El tamaño de la muestra puede explicar la diferencia en los resultados.

lexical_items.meaning_es: a la luz de / teniendo en cuenta
lexical_items.definition_en: Used to introduce a conclusion based on new information.

examples.english_text: In light of the new evidence, the team revised its recommendation.
examples.spanish_translation: A la luz de la nueva evidencia, el equipo revisó su recomendación.

lexical_items.definition_en: Used to describe the degree to which something is true.

examples.english_text: The outcome depends, to a large extent, on early coordination.
examples.spanish_translation: El resultado depende, en gran medida, de la coordinación inicial.

lexical_items.definition_en: To agree with or not contradict another fact, rule or position.

examples.english_text: The proposed approach is consistent with the stated objectives.
examples.spanish_translation: El enfoque propuesto es coherente con los objetivos establecidos.

lexical_items.definition_en: To be considered more important than something else.

examples.english_text: Safety requirements take precedence over delivery speed.
examples.spanish_translation: Los requisitos de seguridad tienen prioridad sobre la velocidad de entrega.

lexical_items.definition_en: To make a conclusion extremely clear or certain.

examples.english_text: The audit trail leaves no room for doubt about who approved the change.
examples.spanish_translation: El registro de auditoría no deja lugar a dudas sobre quién aprobó el cambio.

lexical_items.definition_en: To experience the worst effects of a negative situation.

examples.english_text: Small suppliers often bear the brunt of sudden policy changes.
examples.spanish_translation: Los pequeños proveedores suelen llevarse la peor parte de los cambios repentinos de política.

lexical_items.definition_en: A strong expression used to prohibit an action in every situation.

examples.english_text: Under no circumstances should confidential data be shared publicly.
examples.spanish_translation: Bajo ninguna circunstancia deben compartirse datos confidenciales públicamente.

lexical_items.definition_en: An explanation that recognises complexity and distinctions.

examples.english_text: The author offers a nuanced account of the causes of the conflict.
examples.spanish_translation: El autor ofrece una explicación matizada de las causas del conflicto.

lexical_items.lexical_form: to the best of my knowledge
lexical_items.definition_en: Used to qualify a statement based on the speaker's current knowledge.

examples.english_text: To the best of my knowledge, no further changes are planned.
examples.spanish_translation: Hasta donde sé, no se han planificado más cambios.

lexical_items.definition_en: A software program used on a phone, tablet or computer.

examples.english_text: I use an app to practise English.
examples.spanish_translation: Uso una aplicación para practicar inglés.

lexical_items.definition_en: A named item of information stored on a device.

examples.english_text: Please open the file on your computer.
examples.spanish_translation: Por favor, abre el archivo en tu computador.

lexical_items.definition_en: The part of a device that displays information.
To access a stored file so it can be read or edited.

examples.english_text: Open the file and check the title.
examples.spanish_translation: Abre el archivo y revisa el título.

lexical_items.definition_en: To store changes made to a document.

examples.english_text: Save the document before you close the app.
examples.spanish_translation: Guarda el documento antes de cerrar la aplicación.

lexical_items.definition_en: To enter a system using an account and authentication details.

examples.english_text: Log in with your work account.
examples.spanish_translation: Inicia sesión con tu cuenta de trabajo.

lexical_items.definition_en: To add a newer version of software to a device or system.

examples.english_text: Install the update after you back up your files.
examples.spanish_translation: Instala la actualización después de respaldar tus archivos.

lexical_items.definition_en: To turn a device off and on again as a troubleshooting step.

examples.english_text: Restart the device and test the connection again.
examples.spanish_translation: Reinicia el dispositivo y prueba la conexión otra vez.

lexical_items.definition_en: To join a wireless network.

examples.english_text: The laptop cannot connect to Wi-Fi.
examples.spanish_translation: El portátil no puede conectarse a Wi-Fi.

lexical_items.meaning_es: hacer una copia de seguridad de archivos
lexical_items.definition_en: To make a separate copy so files can be recovered.

examples.english_text: Back up your files before changing the settings.
examples.spanish_translation: Haz una copia de seguridad de tus archivos antes de cambiar la configuración.

lexical_items.definition_en: To tell a support team about a problem.

examples.english_text: Report the issue and include a screenshot.
examples.spanish_translation: Reporta el problema e incluye una captura de pantalla.

lexical_items.definition_en: To start a program so it performs its task.

examples.english_text: The user runs the program from the desktop.
examples.spanish_translation: El usuario ejecuta el programa desde el escritorio.

lexical_items.definition_en: A difficulty connecting a device or service to a network.

examples.english_text: I have a connection problem this morning.
examples.spanish_translation: Tengo un problema de conexión esta mañana.

lexical_items.definition_en: To make a software defect happen again under known conditions.

examples.english_text: We can reproduce the bug on the test environment.
examples.spanish_translation: Podemos reproducir el error en el entorno de pruebas.

lexical_items.definition_en: To formally register a request or issue in a tracking system.

examples.english_text: Please submit a ticket with the steps to reproduce the issue.
examples.spanish_translation: Por favor, crea un ticket con los pasos para reproducir el problema.

lexical_items.definition_en: To remove the cause of a problem.

examples.english_text: The team fixed the issue in the latest patch.
examples.spanish_translation: El equipo corrigió el problema en el último parche.

lexical_items.definition_en: To release a code or configuration change to an environment.

examples.english_text: We will deploy the change after the checks pass.
examples.spanish_translation: Desplegaremos el cambio después de que pasen las validaciones.

lexical_items.definition_en: To inspect proposed code changes before they are merged.

examples.english_text: A teammate will review the pull request this afternoon.
examples.spanish_translation: Un compañero revisará la solicitud de cambios esta tarde.

lexical_items.definition_en: To return a system to a previous release after a problem.

examples.english_text: The team had to roll back the release because login failed.
examples.spanish_translation: El equipo tuvo que revertir la versión porque el inicio de sesión falló.

lexical_items.definition_en: To create an automated or manual check for expected behaviour.

examples.english_text: Write a test for the invalid input case.
examples.spanish_translation: Escribe una prueba para el caso de entrada no válida.

lexical_items.meaning_es: punto de acceso de una API
lexical_items.definition_en: A specific URL and method through which an API exposes an operation.

examples.english_text: The endpoint returns the user's current course progress.
examples.spanish_translation: El punto de acceso devuelve el progreso actual del curso del usuario.

lexical_items.definition_en: The structure that defines tables, columns, constraints and relationships.

examples.english_text: The migration adds an index to the database schema.
examples.spanish_translation: La migración añade un índice al esquema de la base de datos.

lexical_items.definition_en: A defined point separating responsibilities and contracts between services.

examples.english_text: The service boundary should protect the ownership of user data.
examples.spanish_translation: El límite entre servicios debe proteger la propiedad de los datos del usuario.

lexical_items.definition_en: The property that data remains coherent across operations or components.

examples.english_text: The retry strategy must preserve data consistency.
examples.spanish_translation: La estrategia de reintentos debe preservar la consistencia de los datos.

lexical_items.definition_en: A restriction on how many requests can be made within a period.

examples.english_text: The API applies a rate limit to expensive operations.
examples.spanish_translation: La API aplica un límite de solicitudes a las operaciones costosas.

lexical_items.definition_en: The compute, network and storage resources provided through cloud platforms.

examples.english_text: The service runs on cloud infrastructure in two availability zones.
examples.spanish_translation: El servicio se ejecuta sobre infraestructura en la nube en dos zonas de disponibilidad.

lexical_items.definition_en: The future cost created by shortcuts or design decisions that make change harder.

examples.english_text: The team documented the technical debt before planning the refactor.
examples.spanish_translation: El equipo documentó la deuda técnica antes de planificar la refactorización.

lexical_items.definition_en: A decision in which gaining one benefit means accepting a cost or limitation.

examples.english_text: The design has a trade-off between latency and consistency.
examples.spanish_translation: El diseño presenta una compensación entre latencia y consistencia.

lexical_items.definition_en: A method for following a request across multiple services and components.

examples.english_text: Distributed tracing helped the team locate the slow dependency.
examples.spanish_translation: La trazabilidad distribuida ayudó al equipo a localizar la dependencia lenta.

lexical_items.definition_en: A consistency model in which replicas converge if no new updates occur.

examples.english_text: The cache uses eventual consistency for non-critical profile data.
examples.spanish_translation: La caché utiliza consistencia eventual para datos de perfil no críticos.

lexical_items.definition_en: A design in which a system offers reduced functionality instead of failing completely.

examples.english_text: Graceful degradation keeps the core workflow available when recommendations are offline.
examples.spanish_translation: La degradación controlada mantiene disponible el flujo principal cuando las recomendaciones están fuera de servicio.

lexical_items.definition_en: A request that can be repeated without changing the result after the first successful application.

examples.english_text: The payment endpoint requires an idempotent request key.
examples.spanish_translation: El punto de acceso de pagos requiere una clave de solicitud idempotente.

lexical_items.definition_en: The scope of systems or users affected by a failure or change.

examples.english_text: Feature flags can reduce the blast radius of a risky release.
examples.spanish_translation: Las banderas de funcionalidades pueden reducir el alcance del impacto de una versión riesgosa.

lexical_items.definition_en: A mechanism that slows producers when downstream components cannot keep up.

examples.english_text: Backpressure prevents the queue from overwhelming the worker pool.
examples.spanish_translation: La contrapresión evita que la cola sature el grupo de trabajadores.

lexical_items.definition_en: A structured analysis of possible threats, attack paths and mitigations.

examples.english_text: The threat model identifies trust boundaries and sensitive assets.
examples.spanish_translation: El modelo de amenazas identifica límites de confianza y activos sensibles.

lexical_items.definition_en: The range of conditions within which a system can operate safely and predictably.

examples.english_text: The team defined the operational envelope before increasing traffic.
examples.spanish_translation: El equipo definió el margen operativo antes de aumentar el tráfico.

lexical_items.definition_en: A limitation shaped by both technical systems and human or organisational factors.

examples.english_text: The migration plan must account for socio-technical constraints across support and engineering.
examples.spanish_translation: El plan de migración debe considerar las restricciones sociotécnicas entre soporte e ingeniería.

lexical_items.definition_en: An automated or repeatable check that evaluates whether an architecture maintains a desired quality attribute.

examples.english_text: The team added an architectural fitness function for dependency direction.
examples.spanish_translation: El equipo añadió una función de adecuación arquitectónica para la dirección de dependencias.

lexical_items.definition_en: A design strategy that limits how a failure in one component affects others.

examples.english_text: Failure-domain isolation prevents a regional outage from affecting every tenant.
examples.spanish_translation: El aislamiento de dominios de fallo evita que una caída regional afecte a todos los inquilinos.

lexical_items.definition_en: A decision that explicitly weighs benefits and costs using measured evidence.

examples.english_text: The proposal presents an evidence-based trade-off rather than relying on intuition alone.
examples.spanish_translation: La propuesta presenta una compensación basada en evidencia en lugar de depender solo de la intuición.

lexical_items.definition_en: A risk that can propagate through interconnected components and cause wider harm.

examples.english_text: A shared credential can create systemic risk across otherwise isolated services.
examples.spanish_translation: Una credencial compartida puede crear un riesgo sistémico entre servicios que, de otro modo, estarían aislados.

comprehension_resources.title: My simple profile
comprehension_resources.content: My name is Sara. I am from Colombia. I live with my family. I study English in the evening. I like music and coffee. My phone number is on my card. This is my first English class.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify a name, a country, a routine and two preferences.

comprehension_resources.title: At the reception
comprehension_resources.content:
Receptionist: Hello. What is your name?
Visitor: My name is Daniel.
Receptionist: Where are you from?
Visitor: I am from Colombia.
Receptionist: Welcome, Daniel.
Visitor: Thank you.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Recognise the name, country and greeting in a short exchange.

comprehension_resources.title: A normal weekday
comprehension_resources.content: Laura gets up at six thirty. She has breakfast at home and takes the bus to work. She starts at eight. At lunch, she talks with a colleague. After work, she studies English for thirty minutes. She goes to bed before eleven because she gets up early.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Locate times, transport, work activities and the reason for going to bed early.

comprehension_resources.title: At the café
comprehension_resources.content:
Server: Good morning. What would you like?
Customer: I'd like a coffee and a cheese sandwich, please.
Server: Would you like anything else?
Customer: No, thank you. How much is it?
Server: It is six dollars.
Customer: Here you are.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the order, one follow-up question and the total price.

comprehension_resources.title: A change of plan
comprehension_resources.content: On Friday, Mateo planned to visit his cousin by bus. In the morning, the bus company sent a message: the service was delayed because of heavy rain. Mateo called his cousin and explained the problem. They decided to meet online first and choose a new date for the visit. Mateo checked the weather before making another reservation.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Understand the original plan, the reason it changed and the new arrangement.

comprehension_resources.title: Planning a visit
comprehension_resources.content:
Nina: Are you free on Saturday afternoon?
Pablo: I think so. What do you have in mind?
Nina: We could visit the new museum and have dinner nearby.
Pablo: That sounds good. What time should we meet?
Nina: Let's meet at two outside the station.
Pablo: Great. I'll check the bus times and message you.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the invitation, activities, meeting place and one action Pablo will take.

comprehension_resources.title: A delayed delivery
comprehension_resources.content: A small shop expected a delivery of replacement parts on Tuesday, but the package did not arrive. The manager checked the tracking page and contacted the supplier. The supplier explained that a label had been damaged during transport. They agreed on a new delivery date and the supplier offered to send the most urgent parts separately. The manager updated the staff so that customers could receive realistic information. The delay was inconvenient, but clear communication prevented a second problem.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Infer the cause of the delay, distinguish the urgent action from the full delivery and identify the communication step.

comprehension_resources.title: Team check-in
comprehension_resources.content:
Maya: I finished the customer report yesterday, but I still need the latest figures.
Leo: I can send them after lunch. Is anything blocking the presentation?
Maya: Not now. I moved the review to Thursday so everyone can join.
Leo: Good idea. I'll check the figures and follow up with you this afternoon.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify completed work, the remaining dependency, the schedule change and Leo's next action.

comprehension_resources.title: Choosing a better process
comprehension_resources.content: A service team used to handle every request in the same queue. As demand increased, urgent cases waited behind routine questions. The team considered creating separate queues, but that would have added operational complexity. Instead, it introduced clear priority rules and a short review at the start of each shift. The change did not remove every delay; it made the most important work visible and helped the team explain trade-offs to customers. After a month, the team compared response times and revised the rules where the evidence showed unintended effects.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Compare the two options, explain why the team chose priority rules and identify the evidence used for revision.

comprehension_resources.title: Reviewing two options
comprehension_resources.content:
Ravi: We can extend the deadline, or we can reduce the scope for the first release.
Emma: Extending the deadline would affect the training schedule. Reducing scope is less disruptive, provided we document what moves to the next release.
Ravi: What about the reporting requirement?
Emma: That should remain. It is needed for compliance, not just convenience.
Ravi: Agreed. Let's record the decision and review the impact after the pilot.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the two options, the condition attached to reducing scope and the requirement that must remain.

comprehension_resources.title: The value of a clear decision record
comprehension_resources.content: A decision record is not a substitute for sound judgement. Its value lies in making the reasoning inspectable after the people involved have moved on. A concise record states the problem, the constraints, the options considered and the evidence that informed the choice. It also notes what would invalidate the decision. This final point is often overlooked: without a trigger for reconsideration, a temporary compromise can become permanent through inertia. A useful record therefore supports both accountability and the willingness to change course when conditions materially shift.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Explain why a decision record must include reconsideration triggers and how it supports accountability without replacing judgement.

comprehension_resources.title: Architecture review
comprehension_resources.content:
Chair: Before we approve the proposal, I want to separate what the measurements show from what we are assuming.
Engineer: The measurements confirm a reduction in average latency, but the sample is too small to establish the effect under peak load.
Reviewer: So the improvement is plausible, not yet demonstrated at the expected traffic level?
Engineer: Exactly. I recommend a limited rollout with an explicit rollback threshold.
Chair: That would let us gather evidence without treating the current result as conclusive.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Distinguish measured evidence from an assumption, identify the limitation and explain why a limited rollout is proposed.

comprehension_resources.title: When efficiency becomes fragility
comprehension_resources.content: Efficiency is often treated as an unquestioned good, yet highly optimised processes can become brittle when they eliminate slack, redundancy or room for recovery. The difficulty is not optimisation itself; it is the tendency to optimise against a narrow model of normal conditions. A system that performs exceptionally well while demand is stable may fail abruptly when several ordinary disruptions coincide. Resilience therefore requires a more demanding account of efficiency—one that considers not only routine throughput but also the cost of disruption, the distribution of risk and the capacity to adapt without transferring hidden burdens to others.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Analyse the author's qualification of efficiency and identify the dimensions used to redefine it.

comprehension_resources.title: Round-table on resilience
comprehension_resources.content:
Host: Is resilience simply another word for spare capacity?
Guest 1: Not quite. Spare capacity can help, but resilience also depends on how quickly people detect a problem and coordinate a response.
Guest 2: I would add that a system can appear resilient while transferring the cost of failure to users or smaller partners.
Host: Then how should organisations measure it?
Guest 1: They should examine recovery time, the severity of user impact and whether the same failure keeps recurring.
Guest 2: And they should be explicit about whose risk is being reduced—and whose is merely being displaced.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the speakers' different emphases and infer why a single capacity measure would be insufficient.

comprehension_resources.title: A new team member
comprehension_resources.content: Alex is new to the team. He uses a laptop, a keyboard and a work account. His manager shows him the team website and the project folder. Alex opens a file, reads the instructions and saves a copy. He asks for help when he cannot find the meeting link.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the devices, the folder action and when Alex asks for help.

comprehension_resources.title: Ask for help with a file
comprehension_resources.content:
Alex: I can't open this file.
Sam: What happens when you click it?
Alex: A message appears on the screen.
Sam: Please send me a screenshot.
Alex: Okay. Should I close the app?
Sam: Not yet. Let's check the message first.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the problem, the requested evidence and the action Sam says not to take yet.

comprehension_resources.title: A device will not connect
comprehension_resources.content: A developer's laptop cannot connect to the office Wi-Fi. First, she checks whether other devices are online. They are. She then turns Wi-Fi off and on, but the laptop still cannot connect. She restarts the device and checks the saved network name. The problem continues, so she reports the issue with the exact error message. Support asks her not to reset the laptop until they review the settings.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Follow the troubleshooting sequence and identify the step that requires support before acting.

comprehension_resources.title: Support desk
comprehension_resources.content:
User: The laptop won't connect to the network.
Support: Can you see the network name?
User: Yes, but the connection fails.
Support: Please restart the laptop and try once more.
User: I did that. It still doesn't work.
Support: All right. Don't reset the settings yet. I'll check the account and send you an update.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify what the user can see, which action has already been tried and what support asks the user not to do.

comprehension_resources.title: Reproducing an issue
comprehension_resources.content: A tester reported that the search page sometimes displayed an empty result after a user changed the filter twice. The developer could not reproduce the problem at first. After reviewing the test account and browser version, the team found a reliable sequence: open the page, select a category, change the filter and return to the first category. The developer added these steps to the ticket and attached a short recording. The team then wrote a regression test before fixing the issue.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify why the first reproduction attempt failed and which evidence helped the team create a repeatable sequence.

comprehension_resources.title: Daily stand-up
comprehension_resources.content:
Lead: What did you complete yesterday?
Developer: I fixed the validation error and opened a pull request. The tests pass locally.
Lead: Is anything blocking the review?
Developer: I need one configuration value from operations.
Lead: I'll follow up after this meeting. Please add the deployment note to the ticket.
Developer: Sure. I'll update it before lunch.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify completed work, the blocker, the follow-up owner and the requested documentation change.

comprehension_resources.title: Planning a low-risk deployment
comprehension_resources.content: The release plan separates preparation, promotion and verification. Before deployment, the team checks the artifact hash, required environment variables and database compatibility. The new version is first promoted to a small canary group. During the observation window, the team monitors error rate, latency and key user journeys. If a predefined threshold is exceeded, the release is rolled back automatically. A successful canary does not prove that every failure mode has been eliminated; it provides evidence for a cautious expansion to the remaining users.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Describe the release stages, explain the rollback condition and state what the canary does not prove.

comprehension_resources.title: Code review conversation
comprehension_resources.content:
Reviewer: The new endpoint is clear, but I am concerned about the number of database queries.
Author: The list is paginated, and the detail view loads relations only when requested.
Reviewer: That addresses the payload size. Have we measured the query plan with representative data?
Author: Not yet. I can add the staging measurement before merging.
Reviewer: Good. Please also document the expected timeout and the behaviour when the downstream service is unavailable.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the reviewer's concern, the author's mitigation and the two pieces of evidence/documentation still required.

comprehension_resources.title: What the incident timeline tells us
comprehension_resources.content: The incident timeline showed that the first alert was not the initiating event. A background retry process had been amplifying requests for several minutes before the service crossed its error threshold. Because the dashboard grouped requests by route rather than dependency, the team initially attributed the increase to the public API. Distributed traces later revealed that a downstream identity provider was responding slowly, causing upstream requests to accumulate. The corrective actions therefore address retry budgets, dependency-level telemetry and an explicit degradation path. The review avoids assigning blame to the first responder; it examines why the system made the failure difficult to detect.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Explain why the first alert was not the root cause, how traces changed the diagnosis and which system properties the actions target.

comprehension_resources.title: Post-incident review
comprehension_resources.content:
Facilitator: What do we know with confidence?
Engineer: The database remained healthy. The increase began at the identity provider, and retries multiplied the work.
SRE: We should distinguish the trigger from the conditions that widened the impact. The retry policy had no shared budget.
Facilitator: What will change?
SRE: We will introduce a bounded retry budget, add dependency-level alerts and test the degraded mode.
Engineer: I also want the runbook to state when the operator should stop retries rather than keep waiting.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the trigger, the amplifying condition and the three corrective actions proposed by the speakers.

comprehension_resources.title: Resilience is a design property
comprehension_resources.content: A resilient architecture does not merely tolerate individual component failures; it constrains the ways in which failures can propagate. This requires explicit failure domains, bounded queues, meaningful timeouts and recovery procedures that have been exercised rather than merely documented. Yet isolation is not free. Additional replicas, independent credentials and redundant pathways introduce operational overhead and new coordination demands. The relevant question is therefore not whether every component can be made independent, but which dependencies deserve separation given the system's threat model, user impact and recovery objectives. Resilience is a negotiated property of the whole socio-technical system, not a feature that can be attached to one service.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Explain why complete independence is not the goal and identify the factors used to prioritise separation.

comprehension_resources.title: Design debate
comprehension_resources.content:
Architect: We could isolate the event processor completely, but that would add another deployment and a separate operational path.
SRE: Separation reduces the blast radius, although it does not remove shared failure modes such as credential expiry or network saturation.
Architect: So what evidence would justify the boundary?
SRE: First, a failure analysis tied to user impact. Then a load test that shows whether backpressure protects the database. Finally, a recovery exercise that verifies the runbook.
Architect: Agreed. We should compare that evidence with the cost of operating another component before committing.
comprehension_resources.comprehension_focus: Identify the benefits and limits of isolation and the three kinds of evidence proposed before accepting the boundary.
